release_notes:
Fix: Ready alerts silently not received after PCs were left on overnight.

Symptom: in the morning every workstation still showed the others online with no error code, but a Ready was sent and never arrived.

Why: the TCP messaging sockets had no keepalive and no heartbeat (a ping/pong handler existed but nothing ever sent a ping). When a peer slept/hibernated overnight -- or a NIC power-saved, or a managed switch aged out the idle flow -- the connection died with no FIN/RST. The cached outbound socket then became a black hole: sendall() of the small Ready JSON succeeded into the kernel buffer and the bytes were dropped on the wire, with no exception, and the app even logged 'Sent ->'. Nothing healed it, because the listen loop only times out and continues and the peer-sync loop only rebuilds a client when its IP leaves discovery -- which never happened, since discovery is independent UDP and kept the peer list green the whole time.

Fix (defense in depth, fully backward-compatible -- no wire-protocol change, no peer-side change needed):

1. TCP keepalive on every socket, both directions (Windows SIO_KEEPALIVE_VALS, 30s idle / 5s probes) so an ungraceful death surfaces as an error in about a minute instead of the ~2h default.

2. A real ~5s application heartbeat: each client now actually sends the ping the server already answered, sent raw so a dead path raises and triggers the existing 3s-backoff reconnect, and so idle connections stay warm enough that a switch can't age them out in the first place.

3. Liveness-aware reconnect: the peer-sync loop now rebuilds a dead-but-present connection even when the peer returns at the same IP (the 127.0.0.1 loopback is exempt so the local receive path is never churned).

4. Windows sleep/wake recovery: a large gap between the 1.5s sync ticks is treated as a wake event and bounces the LAN to rebuild fresh sockets -- the Windows equivalent of the existing macOS wake handler.

Also: the Ready button now says 'reconnecting, tap again' instead of logging a Sent that never left the machine, and the app refreshes its own IP each tick so an overnight DHCP change is handled without a restart.
